observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.observation_text: Gatekeeper is described as a validating and mutating webhook that enforces CRD-based policies executed by Open Policy Agent; Kubernetes admission controller webhooks execute whenever a resource is created, updated, or deleted.
observations.rationale: Records the documented system role and admission-context behavior without deriving a measurement or classification.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.observation_text: Gatekeeper documentation states that audit functionality lets administrators see what resources are currently violating a given policy.
observations.rationale: Records a documented non-admission observation pathway without inferring architectural conclusions.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Introduction > Validation and mutation, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: Validation and mutation are configured with different policy resources and have different effects; validation uses ConstraintTemplate and Constraint resources, while mutation uses AssignMetadata, Assign, ModifySet, and AssignImage mutator resources.
observations.rationale: Records documented policy resource categories while avoiding component scoring.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Introduction > Validation and mutation, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: Validation evaluates resources and can deny, warn, dry-run, audit, or report violations without changing the resource.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Introduction > Validation and mutation, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: Mutation changes matching resources during admission before validation evaluates the final object.
observations.rationale: Records documented admission-time mutation sequencing without deriving measurements.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: How to use Gatekeeper > How to use Gatekeeper, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: Gatekeeper uses the OPA Constraint Framework to describe and enforce policy.
observations.rationale: Records the documented policy framework reference for the system.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: How to use Gatekeeper > How to use Gatekeeper, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: Validation policies use ConstraintTemplate and Constraint resources to evaluate Kubernetes objects; during admission, validation can deny, warn, or dry-run requests, and in audit mode it evaluates resources and reports violations.
observations.rationale: Records documented validation-policy inputs and outcomes without assigning invariant components.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: How to use Gatekeeper > Constraint Templates, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: A ConstraintTemplate describes both the Rego that enforces the constraint and the schema of the constraint; the schema lets an administrator tune constraint behavior similarly to arguments to a function.
observations.rationale: Records documented contents and purpose of ConstraintTemplates only.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: How to use Gatekeeper > Constraints, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: Constraints inform Gatekeeper that an administrator wants a ConstraintTemplate enforced and how it should be enforced.
observations.rationale: Records the documented relationship between constraints and templates without deriving architecture.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: How to use Gatekeeper > The match field, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: The match field defines which resources a constraint applies to, including kinds, scope, namespaces, excludedNamespaces, labelSelector, namespaceSelector, and name matchers.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: How to use Gatekeeper > The parameters field, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: The parameters field describes the intent of a constraint and is referenced as input.parameters by the ConstraintTemplate's Rego source code; Gatekeeper populates input.parameters with values from the Constraint parameters field.
observations.rationale: Records documented parameter flow without converting it into a measurement.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: How to use Gatekeeper > The enforcementAction field, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: The enforcementAction field defines the action for handling Constraint violations; the default is deny, and other supported actions include dryrun and warn.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Constraint Templates > Constraint Templates, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: ConstraintTemplates define a way to validate Kubernetes objects in Gatekeeper's Kubernetes admission controller and are part of Gatekeeper's validation policy model; mutation policies use separate mutator resources.
observations.rationale: Records documented validation-model placement of ConstraintTemplates.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Constraint Templates > Constraint Templates, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: ConstraintTemplates include policy code in spec.targets[].rego or spec.targets[].code[] that defines policy violation logic, plus the schema of the accompanying Constraint object that instantiates the ConstraintTemplate.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Constraint Templates > Built-in variables across all engines > Rego variables, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: Documented Rego variables include input.review for the request object under review, input.parameters for constraint parameters, data.lib for helper functions, and data.inventory for synced cluster resources used by policies.
observations.rationale: Records documented policy evaluation inputs and helper namespaces.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Constraint Templates > Field Precedence in ConstraintTemplate, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: ConstraintTemplates support multiple policy-code definition methods with precedence rules: legacy spec.targets[].rego takes precedence over Rego engines in spec.targets[].code[], and when multiple engines are defined in code, K8sNativeValidation (CEL) has higher priority than Rego with no fallback mechanism.
observations.rationale: Records documented field precedence without evaluating consequences.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Enforcement points in Gatekeeper > Understanding Enforcement Points, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: Gatekeeper enforcement points include validation.gatekeeper.sh for the validating webhook, gator.gatekeeper.sh for shift-left use through gator-cli, audit.gatekeeper.sh for auditing on-cluster resources and reporting violations, and vap.k8s.io for Kubernetes Validating Admission Policy.
observations.rationale: Records the documented enforcement-point names and contexts.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Enforcement points in Gatekeeper > How to use different enforcement points in constraint, v3.22.x documentation
observations.observation_text: By default, a constraint is enforced at all enforcement points with the common action in spec.enforcementAction; specific enforcement points can use different actions through enforcementAction: scoped and spec.scopedEnforcementActions.
